title: CLR/104/2022 of PRIYA SHARMA Vs GURVINDER SINGH

paras.text:
2024:UHC:9407
1
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Civil Revision No. 104 of 2022

Priya Sharma ..........Revisionist
Versus
Gurvinder Singh and others ........Respondents
No representation for the parties.
Dated : 12.12.2024
Hon'ble Vivek Bharti Sharma, J. (Oral)
 This civil revision is filed by the revisionist to
set aside the order dated 05.11.2022 passed by 5th
Additional Senior Civil Judge, Rudrapur, District
Udham Singh Nagar, whereby the trial court decided
the issue no.3 in favour of respondent/plaintiff.
2. As per the record, the brief facts of the case
are that the respondent no.1/plaintiff filed a suit for
permanent injunction against the revisionist and
respondent nos. 2 & 3; that, upon service of summon,
the revisionist/defendant put in appearance on
18.12.2020; that, the revisionist/defendant filed an
application under Order VII Rule 11 C.P.C. for
rejection of the plaint; that, respondent no.1/plaintiff
filed his objection to the said application; that, the trial
court vide order dated 18.03.2021 disposed of the said
application with the observation that the contentions of

2024:UHC:9407
2
the revisionist/defendant shall be decided by framing
of issues; that, being aggrieved, the
revisionist/defendant preferred civil revision before this
Court, which was decided vide judgment and order
dated 15.11.2021, whereby the order dated 18.03.2021
has been upheld; that, thereafter, the trial court vide
order dated 15.09.2022 framed issues in the said suit;
that, issue no.3 was framed as to whether the trial
court had jurisdiction to decide the suit; that, vide
impugned order dated 05.11.2022, the said issue was
decided against revisionist/defendant, hence, the
present revision.
3. Perusal of the impugned order of the trial
court shows that the court has dealt with all the
aspects of the matter, therefore, this Court does not
find any illegality on the ground that lower court
exercised a jurisdiction not vested in it by law; or failed
to exercise of its jurisdiction so vested; or acted in the
exercise of its jurisdiction illegally or with material
irregularity in the impugned order dated 05.11.2022.
4. Besides, perusal of the order sheet would
reveal that on previous dates of hearing i.e. on
06.01.2024, 08.05.2024 and today also no one is
present before the Court, which seems to indicate that

2024:UHC:9407
3
the revisionist is not interested to pursue the matter.
5. In view of the foregoing discussion, this
Court is of the view that there is no reason to make
any interference in the impugned order. The revision
deserves to be dismissed at the admission stage.
6. Accordingly, the civil revision is hereby
dismissed in limine.
(Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.)
 12.12.2024
Mamta
MAMTA
RANI
